transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Aurora Data, Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Aurora, Platform Eng), Sasha Ivanov (Aurora, CTO)

Summary:
Quick integration discovery focused on which Redwood deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) fits Aurora Data's constraints, integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex SDKs, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks for production monitoring. Customer expressed security/residency concerns and desire for sample code + performance guidance.

Topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/KMS), SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy patterns, request throttling & quotas, observability/tracing hooks, POC scoping.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey, everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Priya Desai: Hey Maya, hey Diego. Good, thanks. We've got about 40 minutes, right? Trying to fit in as much detail as we can.
00:15 Diego Alvarez: Yeah we planned for ~40, we'll keep it tight. Quick agenda - gather your current infra, latency/cost targets, constraints (security / data residency), and then integration approach with SDKs and agent frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex.
00:28 Sasha Ivanov: Sounds good. I'll mostly listen, but want to make sure we don't miss compliance bits - VPC, KMS, SOC2.
00:35 Liam O'Connor: I'll ask the infra questions. We're the platform team owning deployments.
00:40 Maya Chen: Perfect. Priya, can you give a quick overview of your use case and scale?
00:46 Priya Desai: Sure - we do semantic search and a customer support assistant. Current traffic for the assistant is spiky: peak about 150 requests/second, average request ~1.5k tokens (prompt+context+response), embeddings workloads are smaller but frequent. Latency target is sub-300ms for the assistant generation on p95. Cost is a big driver, and we need to know tradeoffs between quantized models on Dedicated vs hosted higher-performance models. Also we have strict data isolation rules for European customers - some data can't leave EU.
01:15 Diego Alvarez: Got it. Helpful. For 150 qps with 1.5k tokens, that's a heavy throughput workload. On Hosted we can route to our EU region and you get multi-tenant hosting with rate limits and quotas; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput for consistent p95 latency, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you network isolation plus KMS/HSM options.
01:34 Liam O'Connor: What does the SDK integration look like if we use LangChain? We already have some LangChain agents in prod.
01:40 Diego Alvarez: We have first-class SDKs for Python and Node. For LangChain there's an adapter we maintain - it plugs into LangChain's LLM wrapper. We also provide a sample LlamaIndex connector. We'll share a repo with examples: sync calls, streaming, and chunked embeddings.
01:58 Priya Desai: Does the adapter support streaming tokens back to LangChain agents? We do step-by-step agent loops.
02:05 Diego Alvarez: Yes, streaming is supported in the SDK. A small caveat is you need to enable streaming on the request and handle chunked callbacks. We'll include the LangChain example for streaming and function/tool calling.
02:20 Sasha Ivanov: For Private deployment, how does the gateway or proxy architecture look? We want to run inference on-prem but still have Redwood control plane for model cataloging.
02:29 Maya Chen: Typical setup is a customer-managed gateway/proxy in your VPC that forwards calls to the private runtime - the control plane is optional to host with Redwood or run locally. In the VPC model we support mutual TLS and customer-managed certificates, and we integrate with customer KMS for keys. We can also provide the option where the control plane is in your network if you need fully air-gapped.
02:50 Liam O'Connor: So we'd put a gateway in front to handle auth, rate limiting and to translate internal IDs to Redwood model versions?
02:56 Diego Alvarez: Exactly. Many customers run an Envoy/NGINX proxy that handles SSO, token translation, and local per-customer quotas. Redwood also supports per-api-key quotas and per-route rate limiting. You can do both layers: local gateway for narrow network controls + Redwood quotas for platform visibility.
03:18 Priya Desai: About quotas and throttling - we need burst capacity and priority tiers for internal product teams vs external customers. How are quotas applied?
03:26 Maya Chen: We support per-key and per-customer quotas and can configure burst windows. For Dedicated customers we also offer commit-based baseline throughput and configurable bursting with pre-warmed capacity. We'll share our quota behaviors doc.
03:38 Liam O'Connor: Observability hooks - we need tracing into our APM (Datadog) and token-level cost metrics for chargeback.
03:46 Diego Alvarez: We emit request-level telemetry and can push traces to Datadog or export OpenTelemetry spans. Per-token cost attribution is available in Redwood Console; you can break down by route, model, and API key which helps for internal chargeback. We'll include the Console screenshots and the tracing hook examples.
04:05 Priya Desai: Any gotchas with LangChain or LlamaIndex versions? We have mixed versions across teams.
04:11 Diego Alvarez: Our examples target LangChain 0.1x and LlamaIndex 0.6x (note: versions in the wild may vary). The adapter is small; upgrading LangChain sometimes requires minor wrapper changes. We'll send a compatibility matrix. Also transcription note: our adapter expects the LLM wrapper that supports streaming and function calling - if you have older LangChain layers, we can show a shim.
04:35 Sasha Ivanov: Security - SOC2 is a hard requirement. Do you have enterprise attestations and how is customer data retained on Hosted?
04:42 Maya Chen: We are SOC2 Type II and provide an enterprise security package. For Hosted, customer data retention windows can be configured; we also support no-retention policies for certain endpoints. For Dedicated and Private, data is isolated and you control retention. We'll send the SOC2 report and security whitepaper.
04:58 Priya Desai: For EU-only residency, would Hosted EU region be sufficient or would we need Private?
05:05 Maya Chen: If data cannot leave EU under any condition, Private or a Dedicated instance deployed in an EU region with contractual guarantees is the safe route. Hosted EU region covers many compliance needs but not every contractual data residency clause. We'll highlight the tradeoffs in the follow-up doc.
05:24 Liam O'Connor: From an infra perspective, we'd want to run an internal gateway and have Redwood's SDK talk to the gateway not the public internet. Is mutual TLS supported between gateway and Redwood?
05:33 Diego Alvarez: Yes, mutual TLS or client certs are supported. For Private deployments, traffic stays inside your VPC. For Dedicated we can VPN or peering depending on the setup.
05:48 Priya Desai: On the performance side, if we want sub-300ms p95 for 1.5k token requests, is that realistic?
05:55 Diego Alvarez: For 1.5k tokens, sub-300ms p95 is aggressive. Achievable with smaller generation lengths or specialized low-latency model variants, heavy quantization, and well-optimized Dedicated nodes. We should run a benchmark - we'll want sample prompts and a test harness. P95 depends on batching and cold starts; Dedicated with reserved capacity is best for consistent p95.
06:20 Sasha Ivanov: Cost question: does Redwood offer quantization profiles per-model? We want float16/4-bit options to cut cost.
06:27 Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Optimize recommends quantization levels and we support multiple execution paths. On Dedicated you can pick quantized model variants; on Hosted we expose curated variants. We'll include a model/quantization recommendation for your workload.
06:41 Priya Desai: Integration question - can we use the Redwood SDK via a private gateway and still get observability in your Console?
06:48 Diego Alvarez: Yes, telemetry can be exported even when requests route through your gateway. We ingest minimal routing metadata (API key, route) and can link it to your tenant. For Private/on-prem deployments, you can push telemetry to a hosted Console or self-host the observability stack.
07:03 Liam O'Connor: Do you have a recommended gateway pattern for LangChain agents and tools that call external APIs? We worry about secrets and inbound webhooks.
07:12 Diego Alvarez: Common pattern: LangChain agents call your internal service that handles secrets and webhooks; that service calls Redwood with prompt+context. Keep secret scope local to your environment. For function calling, you can instruct the agent to return structured JSON and have your service validate before executing. We'll share a sample architecture diagram.
07:34 Priya Desai: What about model rollouts and canarying? We need to roll models with a canary population and automatic fallback if latency spikes.
07:41 Maya Chen: Rollouts are supported in Redwood Console - canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to lower-tier models. You set traffic splits and latency/error thresholds that trigger rollback. Works across Hosted and Dedicated; Private can use the same control plane if configured.
07:56 Liam O'Connor: On quotas again - can we have differential quotas per-route and per-api-key? For example, embeddings high qps but lower per-token budget.
08:04 Maya Chen: Yes, per-route and per-key quotas are supported. You can set rate limits and token quotas independently. We also have alerting hooks when quotas near exhaustion.
08:15 Priya Desai: For the POC, what would you recommend as the first step?
08:20 Diego Alvarez: Start with a small POC on Hosted EU with a representative prompt set and our LangChain examples - that'll be fastest to validate functionality. If latency/consistency doesn't meet your SLA, we scope Dedicated sizing and then Private if residency requires it. For scale validation, we'll run a benchmark with your sample workload.
08:37 Maya Chen: Next steps we'll take - pricing grid, security docs, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, and schedule a SE scoping session. Anything else from Aurora?
08:45 Priya Desai: Please include an example of per-tenant chargeback metrics and a sample tracing integration to Datadog.
08:52 Diego Alvarez: Will do. Also we'll include a sample Envoy config for gateway + mutual TLS snippet.
08:59 Sasha Ivanov: One tiny note - we may evaluate Anthropic for a subset of conversations. How do you compare?
09:05 Maya Chen: We usually discuss model tradeoffs in tone and safety; we'll put some benchmark comparisons but try to focus on integration and economics for now.
09:13 Liam O'Connor: Timeline - if the POC starts next week we want a 2-week evaluation and then decision mid-July.
09:20 Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get materials to you by 2028-06-20 and lock in a scoping session for 2028-06-21.

--- Transcript snippets (meeting body continues, imperfect ASR style, casual speech):
09:35 Priya Desai: so we do have some legacy code that calls openai dot completions, it's kinda spread across services so migration effort is a factor, can we do a drop in replacement with the SDK?
09:45 Diego Alvarez: in most cases yes, our SDK mirrors the standard request fields. there may be small rename changes for function_calling or for tool calling adapter. we'll provide migration scripts and examples.
09:58 Priya Desai: and for embeddings - we see lots of small requests - can batching be done client side?
10:05 Diego Alvarez: yes client batching for embeddings is straightforward; Redwood's runtime also performs dynamic batching if you hit the service concurrently. for embeddings we recommend grouping small doc batches to reduce per-call overhead.
10:20 Liam O'Connor: how's auth handled with internal gateway? we want short lived tokens.
10:25 Maya Chen: short-lived tokens or signed requests are both supported. you can mint ephemeral tokens from your platform and the gateway swaps them for Redwood API keys; we support JWT-based claims too.
10:35 Priya Desai: how will costs be reported to our teams? We need both token-level and per-route.
10:40 Diego Alvarez: Console gives token breakdown, model breakdown and route grouping. you can export CSVs or hook into the billing API for programmatic chargeback.
10:50 Sasha Ivanov: any examples of observability we can copy?
10:54 Diego Alvarez: yes, Datadog span examples, OpenTelemetry proto, sample Kibana dashboards; we'll attach them.
11:05 Maya Chen: ok quick recap - we'll send: pricing grid, SOC2 + security docs, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples w/ streaming and function calling, Envoy gateway example w/ mTLS, Datadog/OpenTelemetry hooks, and proposed POC plan + benchmark harness. Diego will lead the technical repo.
11:26 Priya Desai: perfect. also can you include a note about how retries and idempotency are handled? we don't want duplicate actions for function calls.
11:33 Diego Alvarez: yes, we'll include idempotency token patterns and recommended retry semantics for function-calling flows.
11:40 Sasha Ivanov: thanks - will look out for the docs.
11:43 Maya Chen: thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email and lock the scoping session.
11:47 Priya Desai: thanks all.

Wrap-up (approx 41:50): agreed next steps and action items, end of call.
